summary: Abridgment of Chapter VIII. Tommy reasons out the password, hides in the curtained recess and watches each arrival. Number One appears. Tommy finds the meeting-room door locked, enters the adjoining room and overhears the council through the portière until the unseen blow falls.
acceptable_changes: Reduced the description of dirt and cobwebs to a phrase because it was marked optional.

Cut the Irish-American financing exchange (Mr. Potter, the transatlantic voice, the 'nominally from the States' line) as a unit. Kept the Sinn Feiner's ammunition and 'thanks to our colleague here' line paired with the Belfast quip so the quip still has its trigger.
Condensed the step-by-step handle-turning into a few sentences, keeping the locked-door discovery and the 'dirty trick' line.
Compressed the union report to miners and railways and dropped the A.S.E.
Removed Tommy's list of conspirator types, including the premature 'pale Russian', while keeping V3.
Shortened the German's explanation of the Labour leaders' faith in the Government and of the document's effect.
Added brief source-supported tags in the rapid closing exchange to keep speakers clear.
risks: The word count is an estimate only. It should be near the 1600-word target but was not tool-measured.
The 'thanks to our colleague here' line is kept although the transatlantic speaker it may refer to has been cut. In the abridgment its referent is left ambiguous.
review_focus: Check that the Belfast quip still reads as a reply to the Sinn Feiner's ammunition and money line.
Check that the speakers behind the portière stay tentative (Boris 'rather thought', the commanding man 'fancied') and that no attacker is named.
Check that the shabby clerk-like man and both half-familiar faces remain present and unnamed.
